body:
Indian weddings in the UK mix tradition with British weather: a Hindu ceremony in a temple, a Sikh Anand Karaj in a gurdwara, then a reception in a hotel banquet hall – sometimes all in one cold, rainy day. Here is how to dress right and stay comfortable.

## Quick answer

For most UK Indian weddings, wear a **floor-length Anarkali or a kurta-pant-dupatta set** in a rich colour. From October to March, choose **velvet or heavier silk** and add a smart coat or shawl for travel. In summer, cotton, chanderi and georgette work best. Avoid all-red (the bride's colour) and, at Hindu ceremonies, all-white or all-black.

## What to wear by season

| Season | Fabric | Outfit idea | Layering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Winter (Nov–Feb) | Velvet, taffeta silk | Wine or black velvet Anarkali | Long wool coat or pashmina shawl |
| Spring (Mar–May) | Georgette, chanderi | Royal blue or sage Anarkali | Light cardigan for the venue |
| Summer (Jun–Aug) | Cotton, kota doria | Hand block print kurta set | None needed |
| Autumn (Sep–Oct) | Georgette, silk blend | Bandhani or gota-work Anarkali | Smart trench coat |

## Dressing for each part of the day

**Temple or gurdwara ceremony:** shoulders covered, modest neckline. At a gurdwara, you will need a dupatta or scarf to cover your hair – carry a matching dupatta. See our [Sikh wedding guest guide](/blog/what-to-wear-to-a-sikh-anand-karaj-as-a-guest/).

**Civil ceremony at a registry office:** often more Western-formal. A sleek kurta set or a simple Anarkali works well.

**Reception at a banquet hall:** this is the time for velvet, sequins and statement dupattas. Halls are usually warm, so you can drop the shawl once inside.

## How to stay warm without hiding your outfit

1. **Velvet is your best friend** – it is warm, heavy and looks formal in photos. Read [how to choose a velvet Anarkali](/blog/velvet-anarkali-for-winter-weddings-how-to-choose-style-and-care/).
2. **Thermal leggings under straight pants or churidar** are invisible and save you outdoors.
3. **A pashmina or wool shawl** in a matching or neutral shade looks traditional.
4. **Closed shoes or ankle boots for travel,** then switch to embellished flats or heels at the venue.

## Frequently asked questions

**What should a non-Indian guest wear to an Indian wedding in the UK?**
An Anarkali or kurta set is always welcome, and hosts love it when guests embrace Indian wear. A smart, colourful dress with a scarf also works.

**What should I wear to an Indian wedding in the UK in winter?**
A velvet or heavy silk Anarkali with thermal leggings and a long coat or pashmina shawl for travel.
